requirements.quote:
ClientHello
         + early_data
         + key_share*
         + psk_key_exchange_modes
         + pre_shared_key
         (Application Data*)     -------->
requirements.condition: the client initiates the Figure 4 0-RTT handshake
requirements.required_behavior: include the early_data extension in ClientHello
requirements.forbidden_behavior: initiate the depicted 0-RTT flow without the early_data extension
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized ClientHello extension list can be checked for early_data.

requirements.quote:
ClientHello
         + early_data
         + key_share*
         + psk_key_exchange_modes
         + pre_shared_key
         (Application Data*)     -------->
requirements.condition: the client initiates the Figure 4 0-RTT handshake
requirements.required_behavior: include the psk_key_exchange_modes extension in ClientHello
requirements.forbidden_behavior: initiate the depicted 0-RTT flow without psk_key_exchange_modes
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized ClientHello extension list can be checked for psk_key_exchange_modes.

requirements.quote:
ClientHello
         + early_data
         + key_share*
         + psk_key_exchange_modes
         + pre_shared_key
         (Application Data*)     -------->
requirements.condition: the client initiates the Figure 4 0-RTT handshake
requirements.required_behavior: include the pre_shared_key extension in ClientHello
requirements.forbidden_behavior: initiate the depicted 0-RTT flow without pre_shared_key
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized ClientHello extension list can be checked for pre_shared_key.

requirements.quote:
ClientHello
         + early_data
         + key_share*
         + psk_key_exchange_modes
         + pre_shared_key
         (Application Data*)     -------->
requirements.condition: the client sends application data in the Figure 4 0-RTT flow
requirements.required_behavior: send the early application data after ClientHello in the client's first flight
requirements.forbidden_behavior: send the early application data before ClientHello
requirements.why_checkable: The record and handshake trace exposes the order of ClientHello and early application data.

requirements.condition: the server selects the PSK in the Figure 4 0-RTT handshake
requirements.forbidden_behavior: select the PSK without a ServerHello pre_shared_key extension
requirements.why_checkable: The server's selected-PSK branch and serialized ServerHello can be inspected.

requirements.condition: the server accepts the client's early data in the Figure 4 flow
requirements.required_behavior: include the early_data extension in EncryptedExtensions
requirements.forbidden_behavior: signal acceptance of early data outside EncryptedExtensions
requirements.why_checkable: The early-data acceptance branch has an inspectable EncryptedExtensions list.

requirements.condition: the server proceeds with the Figure 4 0-RTT handshake
requirements.required_behavior: send ServerHello before EncryptedExtensions and send the server Finished after EncryptedExtensions
requirements.why_checkable: A server handshake trace can verify the depicted message order.

requirements.condition: the client sends EndOfEarlyData in the Figure 4 flow
requirements.required_behavior: send EndOfEarlyData before the client Finished
requirements.forbidden_behavior: send EndOfEarlyData after the client Finished
requirements.why_checkable: The client handshake trace exposes the relative order of EndOfEarlyData and Finished.

requirements.quote:
() Indicates messages protected using keys
                  derived from a client_early_traffic_secret.
requirements.condition: a Figure 4 message is enclosed in parentheses
requirements.required_behavior: protect the message using keys derived from client_early_traffic_secret
requirements.forbidden_behavior: protect the parenthesized message with handshake or application traffic keys
requirements.why_checkable: Record-protection key selection is observable for the parenthesized early-data messages.

requirements.quote:
{} Indicates messages protected using keys
                  derived from a [sender]_handshake_traffic_secret.
requirements.condition: a Figure 4 message is enclosed in braces
requirements.required_behavior: protect the message using keys derived from the sender's handshake_traffic_secret
requirements.forbidden_behavior: protect the braced message with another sender's keys or a different traffic epoch
requirements.why_checkable: Record-protection instrumentation can identify the sender-specific handshake secret used.

requirements.quote:
[] Indicates messages protected using keys
                  derived from [sender]_application_traffic_secret_N.
requirements.condition: a Figure 4 message is enclosed in square brackets
requirements.required_behavior: protect the message using keys derived from the sender's application_traffic_secret_N
requirements.forbidden_behavior: protect the bracketed message with early-data or handshake traffic keys
requirements.why_checkable: The record layer's selected traffic epoch and sender secret can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
This data is not forward secret, as it is encrypted solely under
       keys derived using the offered PSK.
requirements.required_behavior: derive the 0-RTT encryption keys solely using the offered PSK
requirements.forbidden_behavior: claim forward secrecy for 0-RTT data or make its encryption depend on a later ServerHello exchange
requirements.why_checkable: The early-data key schedule has concrete inputs that can be inspected and tested.

requirements.quote:
0-RTT data cannot be duplicated within a connection (i.e., the server
   will not process the same data twice for the same connection)
requirements.condition: the same 0-RTT data is received more than once within one connection
requirements.required_behavior: ensure the server does not process that data twice for the connection
requirements.forbidden_behavior: deliver duplicate 0-RTT data twice within the same connection
requirements.why_checkable: A duplicate-record test can count application deliveries within one connection.

requirements.quote:
an
   attacker will not be able to make 0-RTT data appear to be 1-RTT data
   (because it is protected with different keys).
requirements.condition: the implementation protects 0-RTT and 1-RTT application data
requirements.required_behavior: use different keys for 0-RTT data and 1-RTT data so one epoch cannot be accepted as the other
requirements.why_checkable: Key derivation and record-epoch tests can verify separation between 0-RTT and 1-RTT protection.
